prompt:
I need the front end for OneMove. A free national government service that lets anyone who has moved update their address once and have it passed to the tax authority, vehicle registry, voter rolls and benefits agencies.

Who's using it: Danielle Okafor, 29, an ER nurse who moved across town three weeks ago. She's never dealt with most of these agencies directly. She's filling this in on her phone during a 30-minute lunch break and wants it finished without having to call anyone.

What they're doing right now: She's on the second of four steps. Her new address came back as 'not recognized': she typed 'Apt 4B', but the postal register lists the building's units as '#4B' under a slightly different street suffix (Ct vs. Court). The service also tells her that her move changes her voting county, so she has to confirm she wants to re-register there and that her old registration will be cancelled. For the vehicle registry she must enter her plate number, and she isn't sure whether the leased car counts as 'hers'. Then she has to choose which of her six linked records receive the update and confirm a move-in date. That date affects her tax residency start, and it disagrees with a date she gave the benefits agency last year.

What's in the system at this point: Danielle's verified identity profile with her old address (1180 Larkspur Ave, Unit 12) and the new address she typed (77 Wren Court Apt 4B), plus the postal register's suggested match (77 Wren Ct #4B). Six linked records: income tax account, driver's license, one vehicle registration (2022 hatchback, leased, plate pending entry), voter registration (Marlow County, moving to Easton County), a dental benefits enrollment, and a student loan servicer flagged as 'notify only'. Validation results: 1 address mismatch, 1 missing required field, 1 date conflict (move-in Nov 1, 2026 vs. a previously reported Oct 15). The session auto-saves, with 3 of 4 steps unlocked; the deadline note says vehicle records must be updated within 30 days of moving.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
